correctness.rationale: Exact face adjacency count establishes N in {6,8} and its triangle inequality. Polyhedral Cauchy formula establishes piecewise brightness; 24 spherical chambers have exact area arcsin(1/3). Spherical Laplace Green formula with verified conormals gives coordinate moments and weighted cone integral pi/2, leading to E[A;N=8]=3. Total area 12+4sqrt3 yields E[A;N=6]=sqrt3. Classical bounds 2/pi>7/11>3/(3+sqrt3) prove strict negative covariance. Independent 2400 projected hulls, 50-digit cone quadrature and Sobol tests corroborate nonstandard algebra, not substitute proof.

originality.rationale: Neither classical unconditional projection averages nor inspected Platonic/orthotope shadow results determine the two exact area-weighted chamber moments of the cuboctahedron. The full-text closest tetrahedral conditional moment theorem is specialized to tetrahedra; the full-text box section theorem determines only unweighted central-section probabilities. The exact normalized conditional cuboctahedral brightness law and its negative covariance were not found in the inspected evidence, with historical priority risk retained.

value.rationale: A concrete geometric question asks whether higher planar silhouette complexity correlates with greater visible area of a canonical Archimedean solid. The exact integer/radical partition is nontrivial because unweighted silhouette probabilities and unconditional Cauchy means do not determine weighted conditional means; the unexpectedly negative correlation demonstrates a motivated counterexample to naive complexity-brightness intuition.
